title: Cross-Site Scripting in JavaScript
description: A web app renders user input into the DOM with innerHTML, enabling stored and reflected XSS.

finding.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
finding.description: Untrusted content is inserted via innerHTML, which parses it as HTML and executes embedded scripts.
finding.why_dangerous: The browser treats attacker markup as page code, not text.
finding.impact: Session theft, account takeover, defacement, malware delivery.
finding.fix: Insert content with textContent or create elements explicitly; apply context-aware output encoding.
learning_example: textContent renders the same string as harmless visible text

checklist: Encode or escape output in its context (HTML, attribute, JS, URL)
Prefer textContent over innerHTML for untrusted text
Apply a Content-Security-Policy to limit script execution
Validate and sanitize input on the server too
Use a safe templating library that auto-escapes
